images.caption: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge - Nashville's most historically important honky-tonk was a favored watering hole for Tom T. Hall, Kris Kristofferson, Willie Nelson, Roger Miller and other legends who spilled from the Ryman's back door to greet the wee hours at Tootsie's. These days, the room is filled mostly by tourists, college kids and cowboys. It's still a blast to look around, though, even if that glut of tourists and college kids makes moving around nearly impossible night to night. The south side and roof of the Ryman Auditorum are visible behind Tootsie's.

images.filename: AT&T Building, Commerce Street and 3rd Avenue, Nashville, TN (54384169042).jpg
images.caption: Built in 1991-1994, this Postmodern-style building was designed by Earl Swensson Associates for the South Central Bell Telephone Company, which later became part of BellSouth, and eventually AT&T.  The building stands 33 stories and 617 feet (188 meters) tall, and has been the tallest building in Nashville since its completion.  The building consists of a tower with a hexagonal footprint with a podium, including a glass-enclosed atrium, extending to the south, bisecting a plaza at the base of the building.  The tower rises towards a sloped roof with two antennas on either end of the building’s roofline, and is clad in stone panels and glass.  The building today is known as the AT&T Building.

images.filename: Nashville Visitor Center and Bridgestone Arena, Broadway and 5th Avenue, Nashville, TN (54384487819).jpg
images.caption: Built in 1994-1996 and renovated in 2007, 2011, and 2015, this Postmodern-style building was designed by HOK and Hart Freeland Roberts, Inc. as a sports arena and visitor center in Downtown Nashville.  The building is characteristic of late 20th Century sports arenas built in various cities across the United States.
